correctness.rationale: The scheme-theoretic nonbasis presentation and a nonzero A–B pivot put its two columns at (1,0) and (0,1). The equations with these pivot columns kill the complementary components of every remaining A and B column; the only surviving equations are the 2×2 minors of the C block. Their ideal is the prime Segre ideal, giving the full chart A^(a+b-2) × D_(2,c). For c=1 the latter cone is affine 2-space. For c≥2 an invertible entry solves c−1 equations, making every rank-one point smooth, and at zero the tangent dimension 2c exceeds c+1. The pivot minors show that the complementary cross support vanishes exactly when the C block vanishes. All points are covered by cross-pair charts, and different pair-support strata cannot meet. The rank-one cross coordinates identify each support stratum with its indicated Segre product. Completing at zero in the C variables and translating the smooth coordinates gives exactly the claimed completed ring. The projective Segre degree, or the Hilbert numerator 1+(c−1)t at 1 from the degree-d dimension (d+1) times binom(d+c−1,c−1), gives multiplicity c; the chart dimension gives codimension c+1. The two-class case is the Segre product by the same coordinate construction without C. I inspected check_charts.py without executing it: it tests the normalized minors, representative Jacobians and truncated Hilbert identities, not global coverage. The scheme argument establishes coverage independently.

evidence: The earlier record treats general complete multipartite graphs, with an A_i–A_j chart A^(a_i+a_j−2) times the rank-one 2×(N−a_i−a_j) cone, and gives exactly the corresponding disjoint singular Segres with multiplicity N−a_i−a_j.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger record's conclusions specialize verbatim. KLS and Billey–Weaver supply broader equations and smoothness tools respectively; neither was needed to infer coverage of the exact local invariants once the multipartite record was read.

evidence: In the prior chart, complementary rank-one coordinates vanish exactly on the corresponding part-pair support; the chart is singular there iff the complementary size is at least two. Its codimension and Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity are that size plus one and that size respectively.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: On the A–B charts put N−a−b=c and complete at the chosen point, then repeat with the other pairs. This yields every claimed completed local ring and the full reduced singular locus. The two-class Segre and the all-singleton smoothness are not surviving new claims.

evidence: For K_(a,b,c) the edge coordinates are exactly the nonzero basis labels of the positroid. Order labels by the three parts (reorient coordinates if crossing the original cut). On the dense matroid stratum normalize the three distinct column lines to (1,0), (0,1), (−1,1); their ordered cross determinants are all 1. Independent column scalars therefore give precisely the monomial coordinates x_i x_j for graph edges, and their projective closure is the edge variety.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The identification is an isomorphism of the actual projective varieties preserving all support strata. The comparison does not depend on abstract similarities between toric cones.

originality.rationale: The earlier complete-multipartite edge-toric result, Resultary 99655ba7daaa, gives the same strata, transverse charts, multiplicities and codimensions. A cyclic-interval rank-two three-class positroid variety is the same embedded projective edge-toric variety after matching its cross-pair coordinates; the frozen finding is its three-part specialization. This is actual prior coverage, not mere evidence of a similar result or a conclusion from publication-search failure.
residual_risks: The focused public search yielded no usable result; no negative originality inference depends on it.
